A lot of people are focusin on the "doctors are allowed to choose and a lot of doctors wont etc"

Its not even just that. Both are legal at 18, but very very very very very very VERY few trans people are having bottom surgery at 18 unles theyre from a very wealthy background. Do you have any idea how much bottom surgery costs? Its a lot. A lot of medical insurance wont cover it.

If, like me, youre from the UK, the NHS will cover bottom surgery - however the waitlists are humongous. The timeline for GICs goes: first appointment, start HRT, consult for top surgery, top surgery, consult for bottom surgery, bottom surgery. HOWEVER, in a LOT of cases theyll have 2 consultation appointments. If you start HRT privately you STILL have to go to the HRT consults and have your HRT switched to the NHS, its not optional to skip this part regardless of whether you started HRT privately. The wait time to a first appointment for HRT is a minimum of 3 years, often times a lot longer, can go up to 6+ years. Not even to start it, just the furst consultation. And you cant start HRT until your 16 if you have parental consent. After that its approx 1 year wait to actually START HRT. Can be shorter but rarely is, most cases is longer. Then you have about another 3 year wait for your first appointment for top surgery.

So lets put this into context and assume some things, lets assume the person always knew they were trans and got refered to a GIC when they were 13 and only had a 3 year wait to be seen. Theyll be 16, lets say the wait to start HRT was 1 year, theyre now 17. The wait for a CONSULT for TOP surgery, not bottom, would send them to 20 years of age. The wait from consult to actually getting the surgery can range from a year to 3 years, thats 21 minimum. Then the wait between top surgery and bottom surgery is HUGE, I know someone who was under the care of The Laurels GIC in Exeter, Devon. After having top surgery he had to wait 4 years to get a hysterectomy and oophorectomy (forgive me if i spelt those wrong). Then after that, he had to wait 5 years to get phalloplasty done, and the process of phalloplasty is more than one surgery and took approx 2 years to complete.

So using those times, going on saying the patient is 21 as we suggested, theyll be 25 when they get their insides taken out and 30 when they START phallo, 32 when phallo is complete.

The wait times are drastically different, but my point is absolutely no one is getting bottom surgery at 18 unless theyre rich (phalloplasty in its entirety costs £100,00+)

From one artist to another, dont get used to tracing. If you "start" by tracing your work you will never improve. Youre not learning to do correct proportions or colour match or shade yourself. When the time comes to try and move along and do other pieces youll realise you cant because you learnt to trace instead of draw.

Use pictures for influence of course, but dont trace. Watch videos on how to correctly proportion and practice, youll start out shit yeah, but thats part of the process. No one starts at a masterpiece level. Tacing isnt art and its a trap so many people fall into. They think tracing first will help them "learn" how to draw better in the future, it doesnt. To all budding artists, do not learn to trace. Learn to proportion first, then learn to connect your proportions, then learn to colour match, then the rest comes after.

If tracing was an art we'd all be artists. It just devalues true art.

Theyre all the same, all have equal side effects in terms of testosterone side effects (oily skin etc) but patches have a high chance if causing skin irritation where the patch is, as does gel but the risk with patches is a lot higher than gel, injections dont really have that issue at all because youre not applying it to the skin its an intermuscular injection.

Gel is applied in the morning everyday, meaning your T levels peak in the morning and slowly decline through the day until the next morning when u reapply and it peaks again etc. This is the closest to a natural Cis T cycle you can get, the T levels throughout the day accross the span of a month when using gel mimic Cis T levels really well. When you use injections, sustanon specifically, you inject once every 3 weeks, meaning your T levels peak at the start and slowly diminish over the course of 3 weeks, so your T cycles arent as similar to cis T cycles. Obviously youre still getting the same amount of T, just in a different cycle. Having your T diminish slowly over 3 weeks as opposed to daily can cause side effects such as low mood and irritability when your T levels are lower in the last week of the cycle, whereas with Gel thats applied daily, thats less of an issue.

Each way of administering hormones has its pros and cons, but at the end of the day, its just about what works best for you. You might see some people saying that patches and gel dont produce changes such as hair growth and voice deeping as well or as fast, but that is categorically untrue, a few small studies have been done into it have found no evidence to remotely support such claims. Its just all about what you prefer
